instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: A centre-forward with genuinely elite touch and vision who dropped off the front to build play; the finishing was good rather than ruthless.
Athletic, quick, comfortable on the ball and a South Africa regular; clearly better than the Bolton side around him.
Thirty and six starts; the knee injuries that ended his career had taken the pace his game was built on.
On loan from Real Madrid and Middlesbrough’s best player: seven goals and eight assists, most of them from set pieces.
Knee trouble reduced him to eight starts; he was never the same player afterwards.
Thirty-four, seven starts, and the eleven-point Derby side around him; below the level he held at Coventry.
Eighteen, and already the quickest player in the division; the end product was some way behind the pace.
Six starts only; the ankle and groin trouble that wrecked his career.
A miserable season at Spurs with no league goals, but a forward who had scored heavily below and became a genuinely good Premier League centre-forward later. Rated between the two.
Two league goals in thirty-two starts, but the hold-up play and the link were the reason he started every week.
His best season: eight goals, a Europa League run led from the front, and an England call-up at twenty-nine.
A 2002 World Cup star and Ligue 1 champion in his first English season; physically dominant in midfield and a real threat arriving in the box.
Five starts; injury rather than form kept him out of the Everton side that finished fourth.
Four starts across a season lost to injury; thirty, and effectively finished as a regular.
Twenty-one and already an ever-present title-winning keeper; extraordinary reflexes, less command of his box than the very best.
At his peak: thirty-five conceded in thirty-eight, and the goalkeeper Spain won everything behind.
Half a season after a January move; raw, awkward and obviously athletic.
Twenty-four league goals leading the line for a title-challenging Arsenal; a genuinely elite season, and the only one of its kind he had.
Back to ten goals and a season of visible disinterest; the ability did not vanish but the level did.
Fourteen goals as a first-choice starter; the only season he sustained it.
Seventeen, thrown in at centre-half, and physically already a Premier League player.
Loan return after two injury-wrecked years at Atletico Madrid; used deeper and wider, and plainly short of the 1996/97 player.
Three seasons in Brazil in between and a serious knee injury behind him; nine starts back at Middlesbrough at 29, a long way from the 1996/97 player.
Eight goals in 26 starts and the creative centre of a League Cup-winning side; the sharpest he was after the injuries, still short of his peak.
An England cap at 21 and thirty starts in Derby’s midfield; the ability that made him a seven-million-pound player was real, whatever the fee came to represent.
Three starts - the knee and ankle injuries that wrecked his Leeds career.
Nineteen; a big, athletic keeper with obvious raw material who went on to play for England.
Converted from centre-back to striker mid-season and thrived; athletic and quick.
Injuries and a stalled Blackburn move limited him to eight starts across both clubs.
Four years on from Crystal Palace, two of them outside the top flight; a 31-year-old utility defender in Bolton’s first season up.
Ten goals and an England cap at twenty-four; the physical hold-up game finally had a finish attached to it.
Fringe at Arsenal at 21, but a genuine top-flight forward in the making; rated for the player he was then, not the Manchester City regular he became.
Six years on from four Arsenal appearances as a 21-year-old; a settled if limited Premier League forward by 27.
TargetMan rather than AerialThreat: a striker strong in the air, and AerialThreat at 3.5x on a ST decides the scoring charts by itself.

The Kevin Davies profile done slightly better: outstanding in the air, tireless in the press, a genuine top-flight centre-forward without the finishing to be more.
Five starts before a cruciate injury ended his season; rated for the player, not the availability.
Given three starts at 16, which is extraordinary; rated as the raw prospect he was that season, not the England keeper he became.
Ever-present for a fifth-placed Ipswich and called into the England squad. The 1994/95 row is three games by a 16-year-old six years earlier, so the rise is a career rather than a jump.
Twelve starts as understudy at Arsenal, with some conspicuous errors.
Nine goals and nine assists from midfield and City’s player of the season; the one year everything in his game arrived at once.
Squeezed out by City’s spending and visibly off the level of the year before.
